query: I keep writing "reviewers should remember that every new handler under crates/api/src needs a require_action gate" in our PR template, and that note has bitten us twice when someone was rushing. Can we make this un-bypassable instead of a sentence people skip?

We just fixed a bug where a closed case could be reopened by a direct SQL UPDATE that bypassed workflow.rs validate(). I want this invariant to hold no matter who writes the row, not just through the Axum handler. How do I set that up properly?

every time someone adds a mutation handler they forget to emit the audit event and it slips past review. i want CI to just fail when a write path doesnt emit an event so we stop relying on people noticing

Can you write a tools/perm-class-audit/audit.sh that greps type_fields usage and flags any field declared with perm_class but no governing doc reference? Use the flag()/FINDING format like the others and make sure ci.sh picks it up.

I want our 'every create grants the creator an owner edge' rule to fail the build if a future handler skips grant_owner. We already check it informally in rbac-audit but I want to understand how to add a brand new gate dir from scratch and self-test it against a planted violation.

Our docs keep drifting when someone changes a migration but doesn't touch docs/. I want a check that inspects the last commit and complains if crates/ or migrations/ changed without a docs/ touch — there's already docs-currency-audit but I want a sibling that does the same for the OPTIONS schema doc.

Before we turn NUMU_CI_STRICT=1 on in real CI I want to understand what 'a skip is a hole' actually means, audit which of our gates silently skip when DATABASE_URL is unset, and make those skips fail instead of warn.

All four audit.sh scripts fail on ANY finding today, which is fine while the tree is clean, but we're about to merge a branch carrying some known-triaged findings. How do I make an audit diff against a committed baseline and only fail on new violations?

We keep promising in commit messages to 'always reference a Case when touching crates/'. Can we make that mechanical so a commit that edits crates/ but mentions no CASE NNNN just can't land? I think case-first-audit half-does this but I want to extend it.

I'm tightening the rbac-audit R1 regex because it's false-positiving on a helper that takes &PgPool, not State<AppState>. Can you fix the awk so pool helpers are exempt but real handlers still get caught?
Add a new object type 'invoice' to the registry — one type_definitions row plus the amount/due_date/status fields as type_fields. No new table or handler, just the rows.

Why is my new comments handler returning a 403 when an unauthorized user hits it? I expected a leak-free 404. Where in rbac.rs does the reach resolver decide that, and is scope_parent_id cascade involved?
My handler does map_err(|_| StatusCode::INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR) on a sqlx call and I'm getting a bare 500 with no request-id. How should I map this to a proper problem+json AppError instead?
The debuggability-audit gate is red on my branch — it's flagging an .unwrap() in objects.rs. What's the right way to rewrite this handler line so it returns an AppError and the gate goes green?
Add an If-Match / ETag optimistic concurrency check to the PATCH /cases handler so a stale update gets a 412. Where do I read the current version and compare?
I need to add a scope_parent_id to the note type so notes inherit reach from their parent case. What goes in type_fields for that ref, and does the reach resolver pick it up automatically?
Can you write the SQL migration 0010 that adds a covering index on entities(entity_type, scope_parent_id) so the reach query stops doing a seq scan?
Walk me through how the Caller extractor pulls the actor identity off the session cookie in auth.rs and where oauth.rs hands off to it.
ci.sh is failing on cargo clippy with -D warnings about an unused import in field_perms.rs. Just help me clear the clippy warning so the build is green.

We added a DB trigger raising sqlstate NU001 for the cases close-gate but error.rs still maps it to a generic 500. Make error.rs translate NU001 back to the 422 close_preconditions_unmet so a raw UPDATE bypass returns the right status.
